TITLE: Melbourne Cricket Club
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cricket_Club
EXCERPT: The Melbourne Cricket Club (MCC) is an Australian sporting club based at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in Melbourne, Victoria. Founded in 1838, it is one of Australia's oldest sporting organisations and has played a prominent role in the development of cricket, Australian rules football and organised sport in Australia. Its membership numbers more than 155,000.
The club has managed the MCG since 1853, when it was granted occupancy of the present site, and has been responsible for much of the ground's subsequent development. While the MCG is overseen by the government-appointed Melbourne Cricket Ground Trust, its management is vested in the MCC under an agreement extending to 2042.
Although established as a cricket club, the MCC developed into a multi-sport organisation and today incorporates sporting sections in baseball, bowls, cricket, croquet, football, golf, hockey, lacrosse, netball, real tennis, squash, target shooting and tennis; the Melbourne Football Club is also a sporting section of the club. The club fields teams in the Victorian Premier Cricket competition with its First XI being the most successful team winning 22 premierships.

TITLE: Adelaide
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide
EXCERPT: Adelaide (  AD-il-ayd; Kaurna: Tarndanya [ˈd̪̥aɳɖaɲa]) is the capital and most populous city of South Australia, as well as the fifth-most populous city in Australia. The name "Adelaide" may refer to either Greater Adelaide (including the Adelaide Hills) or the Adelaide central business district; the demonym Adelaidean is used to denote the city and the residents of Adelaide. The traditional owners of the Adelaide region are the Kaurna, with the name Tarndanya referring to the area of the city centre and surrounding Park Lands, in the Kaurna language. Adelaide is situated on the Adelaide Plains north of the Fleurieu Peninsula, between the Gulf St Vincent in the west and the Mount Lofty Ranges in the east. Its metropolitan area encompasses over 430 suburbs, extending 96 km (60 mi) from Gawler in the north to Sellicks Beach in the south and 20 km (12 mi) from the western coast to the eastern foothills of the Mount Lofty Ranges.
